subject: CPool<T> handle encoding and internal layout — proven cold from exe
discovery_note: The following was proven by Capstone disassembly of CPools::GetRef at 0x54F420 — NOT derived from any external project. All addresses read from the exe.

pool_struct_layout.description: CPool<T> is a two-pointer struct. The pool global variable (e.g. CPools::ms_pObjectPool) holds a pointer to one of these.

fields.name: m_pObjects
fields.note: Pointer to the start of the object array. Subtract this from any T* pointer to get the byte offset into the array.

fields.name: m_byteMap
fields.note: Pointer to the parallel byte-flag array (one byte per pool slot).

byteMap_byte_encoding.description: Each byte in m_byteMap encodes both the free/used state and an allocation counter for ABA-protection.

bit_7.name: isFree
bit_7.description: 1 = slot is free (available for allocation), 0 = slot is in use

bits_6_to_0.name: counter
bits_6_to_0.description: Allocation counter incremented each time the slot is reused. Prevents stale handles from resolving to new objects.

handle_encoding.description: A pool handle is a 32-bit value. The upper 24 bits are the slot index (shifted left by 8); the lower 8 bits are the byteMap byte at that slot (counter | free_flag). To convert a handle back to a slot index: slot = handle >> 8. To validate the handle: byteMap[slot] must match (handle & 0xFF) with bit 7 clear.
proof_sequence: 0x54F441: movzx eax, byte ptr [ecx + edx]   ; eax = byteMap[slot_index]

pool_handle_validation_pattern.description: To check if a handle is valid: extract slot (handle >> 8), read byteMap[slot], compare lower 8 bits of handle with byteMap[slot] — they must match AND bit 7 of byteMap[slot] must be 0 (slot is in use).

known_pool_globals.note: All addresses from the 1.0 US HOODLUM exe. Pool pointer values change at runtime; these globals hold the CPool<T>* pointers.

CPools_ms_pPedPool.note: Address conflicts with ms_pObjectPool in some references — needs separate cold verification. The GetPedRef at 0x54F420 accesses 0xB7449C with CObject stride (412); the ped pool is likely at a closely adjacent global.

cpools_initialise.construction_pattern: Each pool is initialized with two consecutive `call 0x8207AE` (operator new for pool metadata) + one `call 0x8208BD` (static global registration). 13 such triples confirmed by disassembly.
